players.name: François-André Philidor
players.text: Widely regarded as the strongest player of his time, he also composed more than twenty comic operas. His 1749 chess book stayed a standard manual for at least a century.

players.name: Adolf Anderssen
players.role: Won the first international tournament, London 1851
players.text: A mathematics teacher from Breslau, he won the knockout tournament at London in 1851 and played the Immortal Game the same year.

players.name: Paul Morphy
players.text: He won the First American Chess Congress in 1857 and then toured Europe, beating Adolf Anderssen in a match in Paris in 1858. He stopped playing competitive chess after 1859.

players.name: Wilhelm Steinitz
players.text: Born in Prague, he was the first official world champion. He lost the title to Emanuel Lasker in 1894.

players.name: Emanuel Lasker
players.text: He held the title for 27 years, the longest reign of any champion. He also earned a doctorate in mathematics, and a theorem in algebra carries his name.

players.name: José Raúl Capablanca
players.text: He took the title from Lasker in 1921 and lost it to Alexander Alekhine in 1927. He did not lose a game between February 1916 and March 1924.

players.name: Alexander Alekhine
players.text: He won the title from Capablanca, lost it to Max Euwe in 1935 and won it back in 1937. He died in 1946 still holding it.

players.name: Vera Menchik
players.text: She won the first Women's World Championship in 1927, in London. Masters who lost to her were jokingly said to have joined the Vera Menchik Club.

players.name: Max Euwe
players.text: A mathematics teacher, he won the title from Alekhine in 1935. He later served as president of FIDE from 1970 to 1978.

players.name: Mikhail Botvinnik
players.text: He also worked as an electrical engineer. Anatoly Karpov, Garry Kasparov and Vladimir Kramnik were among his students.

players.name: Mikhail Tal
players.text: Nicknamed the Magician from Riga, he took the title from Botvinnik in 1960 at the age of 23. Botvinnik won it back in the 1961 return match.

players.name: Tigran Petrosian
players.text: He won the title from Mikhail Botvinnik in 1963 and lost it to Boris Spassky in 1969.

players.name: Boris Spassky
players.text: He won the title from Tigran Petrosian in 1969. In 1972 he lost it to Bobby Fischer in a match in Reykjavik.

players.name: Bobby Fischer
players.text: He won the world title from Boris Spassky in Reykjavik in 1972. He did not defend it, so Anatoly Karpov became champion in 1975.

players.name: Viktor Korchnoi
players.text: He never became world champion, but he played two world championship matches against Karpov, in 1978 and 1981. He left the Soviet Union in 1976.

players.name: Anatoly Karpov
players.text: He became champion in 1975 when Bobby Fischer did not defend the title, and he lost it to Garry Kasparov in 1985.

players.name: Garry Kasparov
players.text: He won the title from Anatoly Karpov in 1985 at the age of 22, and lost a match to the computer Deep Blue in 1997. He retired from professional chess in 2005.

players.name: Judit Polgár
players.text: She became a grandmaster in 1991 at 15 years and 4 months, the youngest at that time. Her highest rating was 2735, in 2005.

players.name: Nona Gaprindashvili
players.text: In 1978 she became the first woman to be awarded the grandmaster title.

players.name: Vladimir Kramnik
players.text: He beat Garry Kasparov by 8.5 to 6.5 in London in 2000, without losing a game. He announced his retirement in 2019.

players.name: Viswanathan Anand
players.text: The first grandmaster from India, he held the undisputed title from 2007 to 2013 and lost it to Magnus Carlsen.

players.name: Hou Yifan
players.text: She became a grandmaster at 14, and at 16 she became the youngest Women's World Champion.

players.name: Magnus Carlsen
players.text: A grandmaster at 13, he won the title from Viswanathan Anand in 2013. His rating of 2882 in May 2014 is the highest since FIDE began its rating list in 1970.

players.name: Ding Liren
players.text: The first Chinese world champion, he won the 2023 match against Ian Nepomniachtchi in the rapid tiebreaks, 2.5 to 1.5.

players.name: Gukesh Dommaraju
players.text: He won the 2024 world title match against Ding Liren by 7.5 to 6.5 at the age of 18, the youngest undisputed world champion.
